findings.finding:
R2-2 required the K1 row to say that systemd-boot can append the SMBIOS io.systemd.boot.kernel-cmdline-extra string, which then appears in /proc/cmdline.
- Rounds 3 and 4 said so. Round 5 reworded it to 'is outside it'. Round 6 removes the mention.
- The R2-2 disposition row still says 'The K1 row names the SMBIOS kernel-cmdline-extra string'. That is no longer true.
In v256 the string is still appended:
- boot.c image_start appends it for LOADER_LINUX entries on non-confidential VMs, regardless of Secure Boot;
- stub.c appends io.systemd.stub.kernel-cmdline-extra the same way.
The words then appear in /proc/cmdline. On the enrolled boot they must therefore satisfy the grammar, and through the binding they appear in both entries. So a hypervisor controls part of the bound text. The model is unaffected.

questionAnswers.Q0:
The README dispositions for R5-1 to R5-4 are true in the round-6 bytes.
- rootflags=, rootfstype= and console= are gone.
- The binding is implemented: MAINTENANCE without MAINTENANCE_UNIT must equal ENROLLED, and the unit appears exactly once.
- V67 has its own message, and V69-V76, A08 and A09 are present and replay.
- The environment and widening sentences are restated, and the installed-state list is extended.
Stated guarantee against the model:
- the model enforces exactly what decision 2 says: a closed grammar whose words neither name units nor carry unit-bearing values, with the maintenance entry bound to the enrolled one;
- the K1 row's 'What this guarantees' sentence and the model comment overstate it (R6-1). root= and ro/rw drive systemd's fixed root-mount units, and the binding fixes the initrd= and root= words, not 'the same initramfs';
- I checked one possible split divergence: systemd v256 splits /proc/cmdline with EXTRACT_RETAIN_ESCAPE, so a backslash in an initrd= path is literal. For the allowed characters, the model's single-space split equals both the kernel's (next_arg) and systemd's.
Installed and firmware state beyond the command line:
- the listed items are accurate: default.target, aliases, generators, the init binary, initramfs contents, SystemdOptions and credentials;
- not listed: the kernel image or UKI each entry loads, its built-in initramfs, a UKI's embedded .initrd and .cmdline, and the stub's global credentials, sysexts and confexts (R6-1(b));
- the SMBIOS kernel-cmdline-extra mention that R2-2 required was dropped (R6-2).
Earlier items: no CLOSED item reopened in substance. R2-2's documentation half regressed and is PARTIAL.
Re-run probes:
- E1-E6, M-a to M-c, 50 enrolled tokens (bound), 8 maintenance tokens, G01-G08, G14, G19, G20, GM1 to GM7 and K-a to K-e are refused;
- G09-G13 and G16-G18 are accepted only when both entries carry the same word.
questionAnswers.Q2:
Every v2 rule still holds.
- All 131 v2 negatives and the 4 v2 accepted variants replay.
- R70, R71, L13 and Q07 refuse as the README states.
- The require-level mutation replay leaves 47 uncaught require sites (46 distinct messages), the same set as in round 5: schema pins, data-bound guards, 'migration inputs', both 'profile substitution' checks, and v2 carry-overs without vectors. Every v3 require is caught.
Legitimate hosts accepted:
- A05-A09; C-d (a shared library between native roles); S-c (a leftover unpopulated scope); I-b; W4-c;
- when both entries carry them: L01 (Debian '+' path), L10 (/dev/mapper root), L15 (microcode initrd first), L16 (LABEL=), L17 (/dev/vda2), L18 (no initrd=), and the unit first or mid-line in the maintenance entry.
New refusals by design: the maintenance entry can no longer differ from the enrolled one.
- A separate maintenance initramfs (V72) and another root (V71) are refused.
- GM3 (maintenance without lockdown=integrity), accepted in round 5, is refused. The maintenance boot therefore also runs under lockdown=integrity and the enrolled SELinux words. The W01 §5.5 installer steps (policy load, relabel, fs-verity enable) are not lockdown-gated.
Refusals W03 can avoid: console=, rootflags= (subvol=@, subvol=root), rootfstype=, rd.luks.*, GRUB's BOOT_IMAGE=, kernel hardening words (fips=1, audit=1, intel_iommu=on), PARTNROFF, by-path roots (':'), and a trailing space.
questionAnswers.Q3:
All four facts hold in Linux v6.12. The README digests match the files I fetched at tag v6.12 (7d67e542, c0b27f27, 724cf75e, 362592cc).
- Attach types: bpf-cgroup.h to_cgroup_bpf_attach_type has 28 CGROUP_ATYPE entries. Adding BPF_LSM_CGROUP gives the 29 uapi bpf_attach_type values containing CGROUP, which equal the 22 census types plus the 7 hooks.
- Effective query: __cgroup_bpf_query with BPF_F_QUERY_EFFECTIVE reads cgrp->bpf.effective. For BPF_LSM_CGROUP it spans CGROUP_LSM_START to CGROUP_LSM_END (CGROUP_LSM_NUM is 10). compute_effective_progs carries ancestor programs attached with BPF_F_ALLOW_MULTI.
- pids.current: pids_can_fork charges 1 per task, so threads count, and current reads the counter.
- /proc/<pid>/exe: exec_binprm switches bprm->file to bprm->interpreter, set_mm_exe_file records it, and proc_exe_link returns get_task_exe_file.
questionAnswers.Q4:
Yes. Recording both entries gives the record-level discriminator K1 asked for, and the binding sharpens it.
- Each role and lifecycle capture must report the enrolled entry ID and the SHA-256 of its /proc/cmdline text.
- The two command lines differ by exactly the unit word, so the hash separates them. K-a to K-e are refused.
The statement is accurate: loader-reported, not measured; LoaderEntrySelected is runtime-writable; the maintenance domain is a trusted installer that can reach any boolean state. It is sufficient for an honest maintenance boot, with the pinned booleans and hardening.lockdown as the evidence.
In the initrd, systemd honours only rd.systemd.unit= (main.c), so the maintenance unit takes effect after switch-root.
Precision items: R6-1 (what 'same initramfs and root' covers; the kernel image or UKI and the stub sidecars) and R6-2 (SMBIOS cmdline-extra).
questionAnswers.Q7: Nothing claims a native observation, a measured boot, a selected distribution, seccomp filters or an E01-E12 proof. The 'Not claimed' section and the DATA_CHECK_ONLY flags are intact. The only overclaims are in the boot-entry wording: 'both boot the same initramfs and root', and 'no word ... adds ... a unit, carries root mount options' (R6-1).

reviewLimit:
This is a source-level, DATA_CHECK_ONLY review of the five subject files at commit 946e03c (tree 9ffcbdbd). The files were hash-verified at the start and the end of the review.
It establishes no native qualification. It establishes no kernel, SELinux, cgroup, BPF, boot-loader, systemd, initrd, sysext or TPM behaviour, no installed profile, selected distribution or seccomp filter, and no E01-E12 obligation. It authorizes nothing. A PASS is not authorization for anything installed.
The kernel and systemd facts come from reading published sources, not from running them. Which units an initramfs, root tree, UKI or sidecar ships is W03 installed state.
Repository tests and validators were not run. The v3 model was executed only from byte-identical copies, through my own scripts in /private/tmp/claude-501/w02af-review6/. The out-of-subject working-tree edits and untracked files were not reviewed.
Only the repository (read-only), my scratch directory, the round-5 scratch scripts (read) and public source URLs were accessed. No GitHub, runner, sudo, cloud, native or warm-source action was taken.
